Scope: The package transcribes and audits the published record; it does not reproduce either paper experiment.

A correct H-score can still answer an underspecified question.

HOPE v1 presents its experiments as proofs of concept. That is the right place
to begin: one compression plot asks whether the functional score can identify
useful structure in a pretrained network, and one cross-domain benchmark asks
whether DEFT can trade target plasticity against source accuracy.

The published results are interesting. In Table 2, DEFT has the highest
displayed mean H-score. The paper describes the HOPE compression curve as
superior to the three magnitude baselines over the plotted trajectory.

Neither observation is an exact reproduction, a statistical significance
result, or evidence for one universal framework. The table omits the
scenario-level values and the meaning of its plus/minus terms. The compression
plot omits author-reported numbers, repetitions, uncertainty, and parameter or
compute budgets. The source side of the DEFT score is measured with restored
task-specific state, and the paper prints two different checkpoint-selection
rules.

Part 11 makes those boundaries executable. It does not train ResNet-50, VGG-8,
DEFT, or any baseline. It authenticates the exact v1 paper, reproduces the
arithmetic that can be recovered from the printed summaries, constructs small
counterexamples for the missing aggregation and checkpoint rules, and records
what a decisive experiment would still need.

## Start with the reported record

Section 11.2 evaluates 20 CIFAR-100 to SVHN transfer scenarios: four trials,
each containing five source tasks. Every source task contains the 20 fine
classes belonging to four sampled CIFAR-100 superclasses. Every target task
uses all ten SVHN digits.

Table 2 reports:

| Method | Target accuracy | Source accuracy labeled retention | H-score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DEFT | 89.79 +/- 0.84 | 52.14 +/- 5.29 | 65.82 +/- 3.96 |
| Head-Only | 36.11 +/- 2.79 | 63.13 +/- 4.62 | 45.79 +/- 2.05 |
| Full FT | 94.09 +/- 0.28 | 7.52 +/- 1.63 | 13.88 +/- 2.84 |
| EWC | 93.94 +/- 0.22 | 6.74 +/- 1.74 | 12.54 +/- 2.99 |
| PEFT | 81.91 +/- 0.49 | 5.44 +/- 0.98 | 10.18 +/- 1.63 |

paper_claim (P11-TABLE2-RECORD): under the reported protocol, DEFT has the
highest displayed mean H-score, Full FT has the highest displayed target
accuracy, and Head-Only has the highest displayed source accuracy.

That ordering is a faithful reading of the table. The word displayed is doing
real work. The repository has no task-level predictions, checkpoints, seeds,
or metric records from which to reconstruct the experiment.

## The displayed means do not reconstruct the displayed H-scores

Appendix G.5 defines validation H-score as

$$
H(T,S)=\frac{2TS}{T+S},
$$

where $T$ and $S$ are target and source accuracies.

Applying that equation directly to the two displayed accuracy means gives:

| Method | H from displayed means | Displayed H | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DEFT | 65.9713 | 65.82 | 0.1513 |
| Head-Only | 45.9416 | 45.79 | 0.1516 |
| Full FT | 13.9269 | 13.88 | 0.0469 |
| EWC | 12.5776 | 12.54 | 0.0376 |
| PEFT | 10.2024 | 10.18 | 0.0224 |

The deterministic audit also treats each displayed accuracy as a conventional
two-decimal rounding bin. Because the harmonic mean increases in both positive
arguments, the lowest and highest possible H values come from the two lower
and two upper bin endpoints. For all five methods, that entire derived interval
is disjoint from the displayed H-score's own rounding interval.

verified_fact (P11-HSCORE-AGGREGATION-GAP): Eq. 101 applied to the displayed
aggregate accuracy means cannot produce any of the five displayed H-scores,
even after allowing for ordinary two-decimal rounding.

The discrepancy requires an unreported computation or aggregation convention
to reconcile. One plausible workflow is to compute H separately for every
scenario and then average those H values. The paper does not say whether it
averages by task, by trial, by nested trial and task, or in some other order,
and it does not publish the records needed to distinguish that possibility
from a transcription, reporting, or table error.

open_question (P11-HSCORE-AGGREGATION): what experimental unit and aggregation
order produced each H-score mean and plus/minus term?

## Aggregate means do not identify mean per-scenario H

The distinction is structural, not cosmetic. Consider two records with the
same target and source means:

$$
\bar T=50,\qquad \bar S=50.
$$

In a balanced fixture, both scenarios are $(T,S)=(50,50)$. Their mean
per-scenario H-score is 50.

In a crossed fixture, the scenarios are $(90,10)$ and $(10,90)$. The target
and source column means are still 50, but each H-score is 18, so their mean is
18.

The same two aggregate accuracy means therefore support a 32-point range
between these two valid examples. No operation on the printed column means can
recover which taskwise tradeoffs occurred.

This matters because H is intended to penalize imbalance. Aggregating away the
pairing before publishing the score removes the very information that gives H
its interpretation.

## An undefined plus/minus does not establish significance

Table 2 says that all metrics are averaged across tasks and trials, but it does
not define the reported plus/minus statistic. It could denote, among other
possibilities:

- a standard deviation across 20 scenario values;
- a standard deviation across four trial means;
- a standard error across either experimental unit;
- a confidence-interval half-width;
- a quantity produced by a nested aggregation.

Those interpretations are not interchangeable. The same printed value implies
different sampling units, standard errors, and intervals under each one.
Paired comparisons would additionally require the scenario pairing or the
covariance of method differences.

The exact v1 paper reports no definition of the plus/minus term and no
hypothesis test. Its prose nevertheless says DEFT significantly outperforms
the baselines.

verified_fact (P11-UNCERTAINTY-UNDEFINED): the printed record does not define
the uncertainty statistic or report an inferential test.

The bounded conclusion is not that the methods are equal. It is that a formal
statistical-significance statement cannot be reconstructed from Table 2.

## Source accuracy is not normalized retention

The Table 2 source column is labeled Source Retention (CIFAR). Appendix G.5
describes it operationally as CIFAR-100 test accuracy after target adaptation.
The paper does not report the corresponding pre-transfer source accuracy for
each scenario.

If normalized retention is defined as

$$
R=\frac{A_{\mathrm{after}}}{A_{\mathrm{before}}},
$$

then the denominator is necessary. Holding the displayed DEFT source value
52.14 fixed, a hypothetical pre-transfer accuracy of 60 gives 86.9 percent
retention, while a hypothetical pre-transfer accuracy of 90 gives about 57.9
percent. These are deliberately independent fixtures, not estimates of the
paper's missing baselines.

verified_fact (P11-ABSOLUTE-SOURCE-ACCURACY): Table 2 identifies absolute
post-transfer source accuracy. It does not identify normalized retention from
each source model's own pre-transfer performance.

This does not make the absolute source score useless. It makes the word
retention ambiguous unless the baseline is published beside it.

## The H-score combines two evaluation states

Appendix G.5 does not evaluate source accuracy on only the live target-adapted
model. For source evaluation it:

1. grafts the original source classification head back onto the backbone;
2. masks source-head connections originating from target-adapted slack;
3. restores the original source BatchNorm moving means and variances.

paper_claim (P10-SOURCE-STATE-RESTORATION): this task-specific restoration is
part of the reported source protocol.

independent_inference (P11-CROSS-STATE-HSCORE): the target term and source term
therefore describe performance under different task-conditional states. The
reported H-score is a tradeoff between those two evaluation procedures, not a
single live model evaluated unchanged on both domains.

The distinction should be visible in the result name. A useful future table
would report at least:

- target accuracy in the live target state;
- source accuracy in that same live state;
- source accuracy after head and mask restoration;
- source accuracy after full head, mask, and BN-state restoration.

That decomposition would show which part of apparent retention belongs to the
learned backbone and which part belongs to task identity and stored state.

## The paper prints two checkpoint rules

Algorithm 3 evaluates target validation accuracy and restored source
validation accuracy every epoch, forms their H-score, and returns the epoch
with highest validation H-score.

Appendix G.5 instead says the final run identifies the epoch with peak target
validation accuracy. Table 2's caption repeats the target-validation rule.

These selectors are not equivalent. In the deterministic two-epoch fixture:

| Epoch | Target validation | Source validation | H-score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 80 | 80 | 80 |
| 2 | 90 | 10 | 18 |

Target-only selection chooses epoch 2. H-score selection chooses epoch 1.

verified_fact (P11-CHECKPOINT-RULE-CONFLICT): Algorithm 3 and Appendix
G.5/Table 2 specify different checkpoint objectives, and a fixed example makes
them select different epochs.

The fixture does not tell us which epoch would win in the paper's training
runs. It proves that the implementation choice can change the reported model.
The exact checkpoint rule used to produce Table 2 remains unresolved.

## Data-free capacity is not a data-free benchmark protocol

Table 1 marks DEFT as source-data independent, but does not define the scope of
that label. The narrow capacity calculation reads checkpoint and BatchNorm
state instead of source examples when estimating neuron capacity.

The reported model-selection protocol has a different scope. Appendix G.5 uses
both source and target validation accuracy to choose hyperparameters.
Algorithm 3 requires source validation examples and evaluates them at every
epoch. Separately, source evaluation owns task-specific head, mask, and BN
state; that stored state is not itself source data.

independent_inference (P11-SOURCE-DATA-SCOPE): data-free capacity evaluation
does not make the reported tuning and checkpoint-selection workflow
independent of source examples.

This is not an accusation that source validation is illegitimate. It is a
requirement to name what is independent of source examples and what is not.

## Neuron density is not the parameter objective

Section 11.1 compares compression methods at model density, defined as the
ratio of active to initial neurons across the network. Equation 21 formulates
the compression objective using released parameters and a final parameter
budget.

Those axes are generally different. In a weight-only sequential fixture with
widths

$$
100\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow4\longrightarrow10,
$$

the three matrices contain 248 weights. Removing one neuron from the width-2
hidden layer releases 100 incoming plus 4 outgoing weights, or 104. Removing
one neuron from the width-4 hidden layer releases 2 incoming plus 10 outgoing
weights, or 12. Both actions reduce the hidden-neuron density from 6/6 to 5/6.

independent_inference (P11-DENSITY-BUDGET-MISMATCH): equal active-neuron
density does not fix equal parameter release and therefore does not directly
test Eq. 21 at a common parameter budget. It fixes neither FLOPs nor latency.

The fixture does not claim that the plotted method ordering would reverse at
equal parameters. The author data needed to test that question are absent.

## What the compression raster can and cannot say

PDF page 20 contains one unnumbered 2929 by 1724 raster. It plots test accuracy
against neuron density for HOPE, incoming L1, joint incoming-outgoing L1, and
BN scale on a public Keras ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 checkpoint.

paper_claim (P11-COMPRESSION-PLOT): the paper describes the HOPE curve as
superior to all three baseline curves over the plotted trajectory.

The Part 11 data file is a digitization, not an author numeric table. Every row
is labeled digitized_approximation and author_reported_numeric=false. Its
provenance binds:

- the exact v1 PDF SHA-256;
- the embedded RGB raster and soft-mask pixel hashes;
- the axis calibration pixels;
- the raw pixel range used for every extracted value;
- an accuracy interval rather than an invented midpoint when a trace is
  locally vertical.

The joint-L1 curve has a conspicuous vertical discontinuity near density 0.50.
The digitization preserves the vertical range. Other visible vertical spans
are treated the same way.

At the sampled compressed densities from 0.30 through 0.90, the HOPE interval
is separated above every baseline interval. At density 1.00, the digitized
HOPE and BN-scale intervals overlap. The digitization therefore does not
independently certify strict endpoint superiority across the full trajectory.

verified_fact (P11-COMPRESSION-EVIDENCE-BOUNDARY): the plot provides no exact
author numeric table, repeated trials, uncertainty, parameter/FLOP/latency
budget, or complete reproduction protocol. The vertical label Test Accuracy
does not specify top-1 versus top-5.

The inherited adapted VGG-8 compression run cannot fill this gap. Its recorded
baseline accuracy does not match the surviving checkpoint, so its metrics
remain excluded under LEGACY-COMPRESSION-PROVENANCE.

## Baseline conclusions need the searched tradeoff

Appendix G.5 tunes one representative Task 0 and locks the winning
hyperparameters for all 20 scenarios. The EWC grid ends at
$\lambda=50$. The reported EWC point is close to Full FT: high target
accuracy and very low source accuracy.

independent_inference (EWC-TRUNCATED-GRID): that capped grid does not establish
EWC's best attainable stability-plasticity tradeoff. This is not a claim that
EWC would win, only that the relevant part of its tradeoff curve was not shown.

The same fairness principle applies across methods. A convincing comparison
should disclose winning settings, search budgets, selection units, and full
Pareto curves where a method has an explicit stability knob.

## What this evidence establishes

The strongest defensible conclusion is narrower and more useful than either
uncritical acceptance or blanket dismissal.

paper_claim:

- HOPE v1 describes one compression trajectory as superior to three magnitude
  baselines; the independent digitization does not certify strict ordering at
  the overlapping density-1.00 endpoint.
- HOPE v1 reports one CIFAR-100 to SVHN protocol where DEFT has the highest
  displayed mean H-score.

verified_fact:

- the exact Table 2 values and their arithmetic are faithfully reproduced;
- aggregate displayed accuracies do not determine the displayed H column;
- the plus/minus statistic and inferential unit are undefined;
- source retention is reported as absolute restored-state accuracy;
- the checkpoint rules conflict;
- the compression record is a raster without author numeric data or
  uncertainty.

independent_inference:

- the reported H-score combines task-conditional evaluation states;
- neuron density is not a controlled parameter or compute budget;
- the reported protocol supports proof-of-concept evidence, not universal
  compression superiority, general continual learning, or demonstrated
  parameter efficiency.

open_question (P11-PROTOCOL-IDENTITY): exact task identities, seeds, split
seeds, winning hyperparameters, aggregation unit, uncertainty definition,
partition rule, checkpoint rule, and source-state policy per baseline remain
necessary to reproduce the reported benchmark.

## The next experiment

The missing-experiment matrix in the frozen artifact is a proposed design, not
a set of observed outcomes. At minimum, a stronger compression study should
report exact numbers and uncertainty at equal neuron, parameter, FLOP, and
latency budgets; disclose action types and BN handling; and include prune,
merge, eviction, and combined ablations.

A stronger DEFT study should report:

- pre-transfer source accuracy and normalized retention;
- source accuracy in live and restored evaluation states;
- per-scenario target, source, and H-score records;
- a defined uncertainty statistic and paired inferential unit;
- one declared checkpoint objective;
- trainable and frozen parameter counts, merge counts, and released slots;
- multiple source-target directions and sequential tasks;
- broader regularization, projection, masking, replay, adapter, and low-rank
  adaptation baselines;
- sensitivity to percentile, merge budget, and source-state policy.

independent_inference (P11-EVIDENCE-SCOPE): proof-of-concept evidence can
justify these next experiments. It cannot substitute for them.

## Reproduction boundary

The frozen Part 11 package is an independent deterministic evidence audit. It
uses no dataset, checkpoint, training run, random sample, Torch model, or
wall-clock benchmark. It reproduces published table transcription and metric
arithmetic, not the paper's trained experimental results. Compression values
are explicitly digitized approximations from the authenticated raster. Every
missing experiment is recorded as unknown rather than assigned an outcome.
